title: Cooled-KLL: Enhancing Quantile Estimation by Filtering Hot Item

problem.claim: Quantile estimation is important for applications including database management and network traffic monitoring.

gap.claim: KLL does not account for frequent repeated elements in skewed streams, causing redundant processing and storage of hot items.

contributions.claim: Cooled-KLL is an enhanced KLL sketch designed to address inefficient handling of hot items.
Cooled-KLL introduces a Hot Filter that identifies and stores hot items as compact key-value pairs.
The approach sends only less frequent cold items to the core KLL sketch.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the Hot Filter structure as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The approach significantly reduces memory consumption without compromising processing speed.
Experiments report that Cooled-KLL consistently outperforms five other state-of-the-art algorithms.
Experiments report up to 2.5 orders of magnitude higher accuracy than standard KLL.

narrative_sequence.summary: Quantile estimation supports diverse applications, and probabilistic sketches such as KLL are widely used.
KLL overlooks repeated elements and inefficiently handles frequent hot items in skewed streams.
The paper proposes Cooled-KLL with a Hot Filter for compact hot-item storage and cold-item processing by KLL.
The authors report lower memory consumption, preserved processing speed, and improved accuracy relative to comparison algorithms.

source_observation.claim: Frequent repeated elements can cause redundant insertions and storage in a general-purpose quantile sketch.

interpretation.claim: Separating high-frequency items from the main approximation structure may improve space efficiency.

application.claim: For skewed streaming data, consider a compact frequency-aware filter before processing residual items with a quantile sketch.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the stream distributions, workloads, or conditions under which the reported benefits may not hold.

unknowns: No algorithmic details or parameter settings are provided.
No datasets, baselines beyond the count of five, metrics, or experimental conditions are specified.
The abstract does not report absolute memory, speed, or accuracy values.
